title: Capacity Migration & Graceful Deprecation Playbook for Private Deploys
author: Marcus Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the recommended approach for migrating capacity between private deployment clusters, retiring node pools or hardware generations, and performing a graceful deprecation of deprecated runtime variants. It is intended for Platform, SRE, and Customer Success engineers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) installations. The goal is to avoid customer-visible outages, preserve model-serving SLOs, and provide a consistent rollback path.

When to use this playbook
- Planned hardware upgrades (e.g., MIG->A10032G replacement)
- Data center consolidation and cluster rebalancing
- Deprecation of an old runtime image or quantization profile tied to performance/bug fixes
- Customer-requested capacity reduction or migration to a dedicated region

Principles
- Safety first: every migration has a tested rollback point.
- Observe, then change: collect metrics for 72 hours baseline when possible.
- Prefer live-migration with capacity shadowing over bulk cutovers.
- Customer communication: notify impacted accounts 14 days in advance for non-emergency deprecations.

Key owners and contacts
- Playbook owner: Platform - Capacity & Deployments (oncall: @platform-capacity)
- Primary point of contact: Marcus Chen (marcus@redwood.com)
- SRE escalation: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.com)
- Customer Success notif: Diego Ramirez (diego@redwood.com)

Service-level targets and thresholds
- Target availability (post-migration): 99.95% per-customer over 24h rolling window.
- Max permitted 95th p50 latency regression: +15% relative to baseline for 1 hour during migration; immediate rollback if >30% for >15m.
- Error budget threshold for automated rollback: if error budget consumption > 25% of daily allocation for any impacted customer group.

Pre-migration checklist (must complete before any step)
1. Verify ownership and approvals
   - Obtain approval from product/CS for customer-affecting changes.
   - Create change ticket in Jira: KEY: DEP-YYYY-NN with owner and rollback window.
2. Baseline collection (72h recommended)
   - Metrics: per-route QPS, p50/p95 latencies, 5xx rates, CPU/GPU utilization, mem/GPU memory pressure, KV cache hit rate.
   - Commands: `redwoodctl metrics track --customer $CUSTOMER_ID --window 72h --output baseline.json`
3. Backups and artifacts
   - Export model pin configurations and rollout policies: `rdw config export --cluster $CLUSTER -o /tmp/config-YYYYMMDD.yaml`
   - Save current runtime image digests and quantization profile hashes.
4. Capacity plan and shadow pool sizing
   - Shadow pool should be sized for at least 20% of peak load for critical customers, and 10% for non-critical.
   - Document target node counts per AZ/region in the migration ticket.
5. Customer communication
   - For planned deprecations: notify customers 14/7/2 days before the scheduled migration with migration impact matrix.

Migration patterns (choose one)
- Live shadow swap (recommended for low-risk migrations): create a shadow pool with new hardware/runtime, route 5% of traffic to shadow, ramp to target, cutover.
- Draining-based replacement: cordon and drain nodes for replacement, rely on autoscaler to provision new nodes and shift pods. Use for hardware-replacement where live shadowing is not possible.
- Blue/Green cluster migration: build green cluster, sync configs and data, perform final DNS/route flip. Use for major control-plane upgrades.

Standard live shadow swap procedure (step-by-step)
1. Provision shadow pool
   - Create a new node pool labeled `role=shadow-$MIGRATION_ID` with the target runtime and quantization profile.
   - Example k8s YAML snippet for node pool annotation:

   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Node
   metadata:
     labels:
       redwood-role: "shadow-202601"

2. Deploy shadow runtime and models
   - Deploy identical model-serving configs against shadow pool. Use `rdw deploy --cluster $CLUSTER --node-selector redwood-role=shadow-202601 --tag $RUNTIME_DIGEST`.
3. Start traffic mirroring (no client impact)
   - Enable passive mirroring: use the traffic-router flag `--mirror-only` for 24h to validate inference parity and throughput.
   - Commands: `traffic-router configure --cluster $CLUSTER --mirror-to shadow-202601 --mirror-rate 0.05`
4. Validate observability and correctness
   - Run the parity test harness: `eval-harness run --suite smoke --target shadow-202601 --compare baseline.json`
   - Check for model output drift, latency regressions, and increased 5xx rates.
5. Ramp traffic to shadow
   - Ramp in increments: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over a minimum of 2 hours between ramps.
   - After each ramp, wait 30 minutes to validate SLOs. If p95 latency > threshold, pause and investigate.
6. Final cutover or failback
   - If all checks pass at 100% for 1 hour, update routing policy to make shadow the new primary.
   - If issues detected, immediately revert routing to previous primary and trigger the rollback checklist below.

Rollback checklist (fast path)
- Trigger conditions:
  - p95 latency > 30% above baseline for >15m
  - Error rates exceed 3x baseline for >10m
  - Customer-reported critical failures

Immediate rollback actions:
1. Pause traffic ramp and shift 100% back to previous pool: `traffic-router set-primary --cluster $CLUSTER --pool primary-1`
2. Mark migration as failed in Jira ticket and capture investigation artifacts (logs, traces, perf snapshots).
3. Start post-failure triage: open incident channel on #platform-incidents and assign SRE owners.

Post-migration validation (24–72h)
- Verify: per-customer SLOs, model response parity, KV cache warmup, autoscaler behavior, and any billing/regression impacts.
- Run targeted canary evals against production traffic samples to confirm output quality.

Deprecation-specific guidance
- When deprecating a runtime image or quantization profile: create a deprecation RFC page and include product/CS approvals.
- Soft deprecation (90 days): remove new deployments from using the variant, leave it available but unsupported.
- Hard deprecation (180 days): evict from all clusters after providing migration tooling (automated `rdw migrate-runtime` job) and customer migration paths.

Customer-facing templates
- 14-day notice email subject: "Action required: Migration of your Redwood private deployment"
- Example short body: "We will begin migrating model-serving capacity for your cluster on YYYY-MM-DD. Expected impact: brief warm-up of caches; no expected downtime. Contact your CS rep if you require a maintenance window."

Configuration and minimal requirements table
- | Item | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
  | Node GPU | 1x A100 40GB | 2x A100 80GB | Shadow pools should match or exceed primary capacity |
  | Runtime image | redwood/runtime:v2025-11 | redwood/runtime:v2026-01 | Pin by digest in migration tickets |
  | Quant profile | q8_256 | q4f_128 | Test output parity before switching |

Automations and tooling
- rdw-migrate-job: a scheduled job that can migrate runtime pins across clusters with a dry-run mode. Usage: `rdw-migrate-job --src-cluster old --dst-cluster new --dry-run`
- traffic-router: supports mirror, gradual ramp, and immediate failback commands. See `traffic-router --help` for flags.

Postmortem and learnings
- For any migration with a customer-facing incident, create a postmortem within 48 hours. Include timeline, root cause, and 3 action items with owners and target dates.

Appendix A — Quick commands
- Export config: `rdw config export --cluster $CLUSTER -o /tmp/config.yaml`
- Start mirror: `traffic-router configure --cluster $CLUSTER --mirror-to $POOL --mirror-rate 0.05`
- Promote shadow: `traffic-router set-primary --cluster $CLUSTER --pool $POOL`

Appendix B — Example Jira checklist (copy into ticket)
1. Pre-approval obtained (product/CS)
2. Baseline metrics attached
3. Shadow pool provisioned
4. Mirror validated for 24h
5. Ramp schedule added
6. Rollback verified and tested
7. Customer notifications sent
